Subject: Post-demo: pen-test artifacts, SLA & disclosure path (next steps)

Hi Sanjay / Riley —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the clear context around your PHI scope and the two apps you plan to integrate with Redwood. A couple of follow-ups from our side so your security team has what it needs to triage: 

Summary of asks from your security intake: 
- SOC 2 status and in-scope systems (you asked if we have recent AICPA report and control owner contacts)
- HIPAA posture for the hosted API (BAA & data flow diagrams)
- Pen test: delivery of prior summary report (redacted if necessary), and preferred method for receiving a new test result (S3 link, secure portal, or gated email)
- Vulnerability management: SLA expectations for triage/remediation, scanning cadence (internal & external), and disclosure notification process to customers

Next steps on our side (proposed): 
1) I'll share our SOC 2 summary and the BAA + paste of our security contact. Monica — can you attach the latest SOC 2 summary and the BAA (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf)?
2) Marissa / Ben — please review the pen intake form and propose a minimal artifact set we can supply up front (pen-intake-form.pdf attached).
3) Sanjay — confirm whether Acme prefers a secure S3 upload (pre-signed link + ephemeral credentials) or an encrypted DocShare for report exchange. We can also redact customer-identifying data if you prefer.

Timing: if we can align by next Wednesday (12/16) on the delivery method and NDA/handback expectations, Ben can coordinate with your QSA to schedule the pen and provide timeline SLAs.

Attachment: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (high-level milestones / who-does-what).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman

Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pen-test artifacts, SLA & disclosure path (next steps)

Thanks Naomi — adding a couple of technical clarifications for Acme's security team: 

1) SOC 2: we completed Type II audit in 2026-07; the full report is under NDA. The attached PDF (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) includes our control owner list and a summary of exceptions (none open). If Acme's legal wants the full report, we can provide it after an executed NDA/handshake agreement.

2) HIPAA / BAA: we have a standard BAA; I'll attach a copy and highlight the data flow diagrams that show PHI egress (we do not persist PHI beyond ephemeral caching unless explicitly configured).

3) Pen test handback: our standard is to deliver an executive summary publicly and the full findings under NDAs to customers or their auditors. For high-severity (P1/P0) findings, we commit to a 72-hour acknowledgement and 30-day remediation SLA where feasible. For lower severity items, we batch fixes into the next maintenance window.

4) Scanning cadence: we run internal SAST/DAST monthly and external authenticated scans quarterly; we also run retroactive scans on major releases. We use a staged disclosure policy: 1) notify affected customer contacts when exploitability is confirmed, 2) public advisory only after patches are available or mitigations are in place.

Ben — please confirm the exact cadence for external authenticated scans and whether we can offer Acme a tighter SLA under Dedicated/Private plans.

Monica Patel
Sr. Security PM | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmehealth.com>, Riley O'Connor <riley.oc@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pen-test artifacts, SLA & disclosure path (next steps)

Hi Sanjay / Riley —

Ben from Redwood security here. Short answers and an action list so the Acme team has what to plan for: 

- Preferred transfer: pre-signed S3 link with KM-encrypted bundle (we'll set expiry at 7 days unless you request shorter). We can also provide a one-time password-encrypted ZIP via our secure portal.
- Redaction: we will redact internal customer identifiers on request; however if your QSA needs full context we'll request a specific redaction list to avoid losing triage data.
- SLA: for confirmed P1/P0 issues we will acknowledge within 72 hours and provide a remediation plan within 14 calendar days. We can negotiate an accelerated 7-day remediation plan as part of a Dedicated capacity contract (per your compliance needs).
- Scan cadence: external authenticated quarterly; internal monthly. If you'd like weekly external scans during onboarding we can run a four-week ramp for the initial engagement.

Action items: 
1) Acme: confirm transfer preference (S3 vs portal) and whether you'd like redaction (and to what level).
2) Acme: sign the temporary NDA (DocuSign link sent separately) if you want the full report.
3) Redwood (Marissa): prepare a trimmed artifact bundle (scope, environment matrix, public exec summary) and a statement of remediation SLAs that we can include in the MAP.

Sanjay / Riley — if you prefer a 1:1 technical call between your QSA and our security folks, we can schedule next week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pen-test artifacts, SLA & disclosure path (next steps)

Thanks all — useful summary. A few quick points from Acme Security: 

1) Transfer: S3 pre-signed link preferred. Please set expiry to 48 hours. We will request the full (unredacted) report under NDA; in parallel, a redacted executive summary to share with compliance.
2) SLA: 72-hour acknowledgement is fine. For remediation, we prefer a 14-day plan for P1 and 45 days for P2 unless both parties agree otherwise. We are open to accelerated timelines if Redwood can commit under a Dedicated agreement.
3) Scan cadence: quarterly external scans acceptable for steady-state. We would like weekly scans for the first month after go-live.

We'll execute the temporary NDA this afternoon and upload our pen intake template for context. Looking forward to the next steps.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Director of Security Operations | Acme Health
sanjay@acmehealth.com
